transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-04-14 15:00 UTC — Duration 42m. Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Derek (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood), Dr. Elena Ortiz (MosaicLab CTO), Samir Khan (Head of Platform), Priya Nair (SRE).

Summary: quick bench scrub of week-3 results, focused on latency delta vs their incumbent (IncumbentAI), throughputs at 8k and 32k context, and routing/fallback behaviour during spikes. Action items and canary scheduling captured.

Topics: benchmark histograms, p95/p99 deltas, KV cache hit rate, batching and quantization tradeoffs, dedicated slot request for 10-2pm PST window, security checklist for pilot.

--- Transcript body ---
00:00 Maya: alright team thanks for joining, uh we'll try to keep to 40 minutes. quick status check — did everyone get the latest bench CSV?
00:07 Elena: yes got it, skimmed it. looks like the p99 numbers are smaller this week but still higher than incumbent in long-context.
00:15 Derek: right so quick notes — we tuned batching and pushed a different quant profile (8bit-mq) for the LLM during the 32k tests. that shaved the median by about 18% but the tail is... still sticky.
00:30 Samir: sticky meaning p99? like what's the delta vs IncumbentAI at 32k?
00:36 Derek: on our run, p50 was 220ms lower, p95 roughly 320ms lower, p99 is about 700ms lower for short prompts (<=8k). at 32k we see p95 is only about 120ms lower and p99 actually edges about +180ms versus incumbent in two of the runs — likely related to KV cache miss storms and page faults during long KV lookups.
00:58 Priya: we saw some blips in SRE logs where memory pressure caused a GC-like pause on their test harness, could be an artifact of the orchestrator too.
01:08 Luis: note we also had different routing — some fraction was routed to the fallback quantized variant which increases per-token compute slightly; that may affect tail.
01:16 Elena: can you explain the fallback routing? is that something we can disable for the canary?
01:22 Derek: yes it's policy-driven — default is latency-optimized with fallback to lower-precision when capacity tightens. we can pin to the same model variant across the canary window, or we can ensure the fallback threshold is higher so it doesn't trigger at expected load.
01:35 Samir: for baseline comparison fairness we need identical model variants and cache warm state. Incumbent was running a 16-bit FP baseline with aggressive prefix caching; how close can Redwood get?
01:46 Derek: we can run a 16-bit path as well, but our 8-bit-mq gives cost benefits. for apples-to-apples, we can schedule a straight 16-bit run with explicit prefix warming — we used a synthetic warm-up but maybe not identical to their warm-up pattern.
02:01 Maya: quick interjection — the customer asked for per-route histograms, and we added them into the sheet. Derek can you call out the key per-route takeaways?
02:09 Derek: sure. Route A (short task routing) shows consistent 30-40% throughput improvement and much lower median. Route B (long context, multi-turn) shows more variance; throughput is similar but tail spikes are more frequent when our KV cache has churn. Hit rate on the KV cache during the 32k runs dropped to ~68% on one test which correlated with p99 spikes.
02:35 Priya: what causes the KV cache churn? is it sequence length distribution or concurrency?
02:40 Derek: both — high concurrency with varied prefixes evicts warm entries. we recommend prefix bucketing (group similar prefixes at ingress) and slightly larger cache allocation for the pilot. we can bump cache allocation for your dedicated slot.
02:50 Samir: allocation meaning memory per instance? will that cost extra?
02:54 Luis: yes it's memory on the serving nodes; in Dedicated mode that's configurable and we can propose a delta in reserved capacity or use our burst capacity for the canary period. Maya: pricing note captured in action items.
03:08 Elena: another datapoint — the incumbent uses synchronous batching with fixed batch sizes. Redwood's continuous batching is different; how did that show up in the benchmarks?
03:18 Derek: continuous batching gives lower median for diverse workloads but can lead to slightly higher tails for very long contexts if batches starve or if KV misses prolong per-token time. we experimented with max batch delay and saw a p95 improvement of ~90ms when reducing delay from 8ms to 4ms, but throughput dropped 6%. it's a tradeoff.
03:42 Samir: can you produce a short sensitivity table? like p95 vs batch-delay and throughput % impact so we can choose operating point?
03:48 Derek: yeah we'll export that tomorrow — expect a 3-row table: 2ms, 4ms, 8ms.
03:55 Priya: security question — will the canary traffic stay in our VPC and send logs to our SIEM? we need to validate no egress to public buckets.
04:03 Maya: yes for the Private pilot we can ensure logs and telemetry flow to your SIEM via the VPC peering; Derek will validate the log sink configuration.
04:12 Elena: on the p99 tail — is it consistent run-to-run or intermittent?
04:16 Derek: intermittent. we reproduced it twice out of five 32k runs. looking at thread dumps suggests a kernel scheduling pause when memory hot-swap happens — may be mitigated by tuning slab alloc and increasing page cache. we'll coordinate with your infra.
04:30 Samir: ok let's talk about the dedicated slot request — we asked for daytime capacity 10-14 PST for 48 hours; what's the ETA?
04:36 Luis: we can provision a reserved slot in the next 36 hours, pending purchase order. if you need immediate testing we can burst into our shared pool but that doesn't guarantee identical perf.
04:47 Maya: procurement signal? Elena: you mentioned internal approvals this week?
04:52 Elena: yes finance is reviewing the pilot paperwork, should be approved early next week.
04:56 Samir: if procurement is slower, can Redwood still run the canary with 10% traffic via hosted? we want to validate real traffic patterns.
05:04 Maya: yes hosted canary is doable; we'd need the API keys and routing rule. Derek: caveat on data retention — hosted data will be captured in our analytics unless we enable strict no-retain for the pilot, which we can do.
05:18 Priya: please send SOC2 and encryption docs again. we redacted earlier copy from the last pack.
05:24 Maya: will do after call.
05:26 --- brief silence, then back to bench specifics ---
05:30 Derek: one more note — quantization profile: the 8bit-mq variant reduces compute by ~28% and cost by about 24% in our estimator, but it amplifies tail on long contexts in some workloads. we can tune the quant table (per-layer thresholds) to smooth the tail; that'll be our next engineering spike if you want us to prioritize.
05:50 Elena: yes prioritize tail smoothing, but document the exact delta so we can run A/B. also add test harness scripts to reproduce.
06:00 Derek: will provide harness and seed inputs.
06:05 Maya: great. quick recap on next steps and owners?
06:09 Elena: go ahead Maya.
06:10 Maya: re-iterating: Redwood shares per-route histograms + p95/p99 CSV by Friday (Derek to do), export of batch-delay sensitivity table, pricing and pilot billing (Maya), dedicated slot ETA and config (Luis), security/soc2 docs and log sink plan (Maya/Derek), MosaicLab will run the 100k token baseline test and share logs, and approve PO if finance clears.
06:36 Samir: timeline sounds good. schedule the 48hr canary tentatively for 2027-04-21 pending PO.
06:44 Priya: I'll send SRE creds for log forwarding by EOD Sunday.
06:49 Maya: perfect thanks all.
06:51 Elena: thanks everyone, useful sync.
06:53 Meeting end.

Notes about transcription: occasional mislabels and filler words retained; technical jargon kept intact though acronym expansions may be approximate (KV cache sometimes transcribed as K V cache, quantization shows as quant table).
